narration: Multi-view input images I-one-to-K and their object masks M-one-to-K define the capture of the scene containing the bear statue.
These views are fit into a 3D Gaussian splatting representation G-one-to-N of the full scene.
Rendering depth from the Gaussians yields the per-view depth maps D-one-to-K, completing the Gaussians-with-bear-statue stage.
Two reference views are selected: image I-two with mask M-two, and image I-one with mask M-one.
Masking each image by its object mask produces the background-only images I-B-two and I-B-one.
Using depth D-two, view two is projected into view one and merged, giving the combined background image I-B-one-two.
Where the merged background is still unknown, the refined inpainting mask M-prime-one is derived.
Guided by M-prime-one, the reference view is inpainted to give the inpainted image I-In-one and its depth D-In-one.
The refined depth D-prime-one and image I-prime-one are compared with the inpainted pair through the render loss L-render.
Rendering the reference view xi-one back from the refined Gaussians G-prime-one-to-N-prime closes the single-view loop.
A depth-guided projection builds the point cloud P-one, which initializes the refined Gaussian field G-prime.
Projecting to other views and rendering views xi-two-to-K lets the cross loss L-cross align I-P-two-to-K with I-prime-two-to-K, finishing the inpainting-guided 3DGS refinement.
